blind_target.evidence_quote: While we replicate the experiments of PZ and ILS as closely as possible and use features of their setup to identify subject misconceptions, Bartling et al. (forthcoming) focus on the claim in Cason and Plott (2014) that misconceptions about the BDM can be falsely interpreted as support for theories of framing, such as reference-dependent preferences.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Thus, we are not able to replicate the results on the valuations of mugs by PZ and ILS.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit failure verdict for the central mug valuation finding. Agreement in training lottery tasks does not overturn the failure of the focal effect.

luna_triage.reason: The paper explicitly says it replicates the experiments of PZ and ILS, then contrasts its mug valuation results with those of both and states it cannot replicate the mug valuation results. The Isoni, Loomes, and Sugden 2011 comment is separately identified in the source reference list; supplied row 2519 is only Plott and Zeiler (2005), so it does not represent the separately published ILS paper. The retested finding is that extensive instructions and training remove the WTP–WTA gap in the classic mug experiment.
luna_triage.omission_quote: Thus, we are not able to replicate the results on the valuations of mugs by PZ and ILS.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Consistent with PZ, though, they find no gap in their classic mug experiment. Although both PZ and ILS show that the WTP–WTA gap in the classic mug experiment disappears if subjects receive extensive instructions and training,
